name: Tomato Leaf Miner
description: Small fly larvae that tunnel through tomato leaves, creating serpentine mines. Tuta absoluta (tomato pinworm) is particularly destructive, also mining stems and boring into fruits, causing extensive damage.
symptoms: Serpentine winding tunnels visible within leaf tissue
Mines starting as narrow and widening as larvae grow
Leaf tissue turning brown and necrotic along mines
Fruit entry holes with frass (Tuta absoluta)
Leaf desiccation and death in severe infestations
treatments: Apply spinosad or abamectin at first signs of mining
Remove and destroy infested leaves (for minor infestations)
Use neem oil or Bacillus thuringiensis for young larvae
Install pheromone traps for Tuta absoluta monitoring and mass trapping
Apply chlorantraniliprole for severe Tuta infestations
prevention: Use insect-proof nets in seedling nurseries
Remove weed hosts that harbor leaf miners
Practice crop rotation with non-host crops
Conserve natural enemies (parasitic wasps, predatory bugs)
Install yellow sticky traps for monitoring adult flies
